call.prompt:
You recommend one board game. You get a person's request and five candidate
games, A to E. Each game has a fact card and a description.

Pick one game that meets every requirement in the request. If no game meets
every requirement, decline. Never pick the closest match.

GENERAL RULES
- Use only the game's card and description. Ignore anything else you know
  about the game.
- A wish is not a requirement. "Would be nice", "would be amazing", "we'd
  love", "bonus points for" and "similar to ..." mark wishes. Ignore them,
  even when the wish is about something below, such as co-op.
- If the request says nothing about a kind of requirement, or says it
  doesn't matter, there is no requirement of that kind.
- If you can't check a requirement from the card or the description, the
  game can't be picked.
- When players, play time, age or complexity is "not listed", only the
  description can answer it. When categories or mechanics are "not listed",
  the game simply has no tags there.

REQUIREMENTS

Players. Count everyone who plays, including the writer: "me and my three
friends" is 4, "game night with six friends" is 7. The number must be inside
the card's player range. A player count that needs an expansion doesn't count.

Play time. Turn the phrase into a limit in minutes. "An hour", "an hour
tops" and "about an hour" mean at most 60. "Half an hour" means at most 30.
"Two hours at most" means at most 120. The game's longest listed time must
be within the limit, so "30 to 60 minutes" doesn't fit "at most 45". The
time to learn the rules is not play time.

Complexity. "Easy rules", "simple", "beginners" and "casual players" ask for
light. "Deep strategy", "meaty" and "nothing light" ask for heavy. "Not too
simple, not too heavy" asks for medium. Use the card's complexity weight
(1 to 5), its game types, and what the description says about how hard the
rules are.
- Light: yes if the weight is 1.3 or less, or the description says the rules
  are easy or simple, or it is a children's or party game, or it is a family
  game with a weight under 2.0. No if the weight is 4.0 or more, or the
  description says the rules are complex or for experienced players, or its
  only types are strategy, thematic, war or abstract and the weight is 2.5
  or more.
- Heavy: yes if the weight is 4.0 or more, or the description says the rules
  are complex or for experienced players, or it is a strategy or war game,
  not also a family game, with a weight of 3.5 or more. No if the weight is
  1.3 or less, or the description says the rules are easy or simple, or it
  is a children's, party or family game.
- Medium: yes if the game is neither light nor heavy and its weight is
  between 2.0 and 3.5.
- A weight of 1.3 or less, or 4.0 or more, wins over every other clue. If
  the clues point both ways, or none applies, you can't tell.
- "Easy to learn but hard to master" decides nothing. Wording about how hard
  the game is to win, or who it is marketed to, doesn't count.

Cooperative or competitive. "Together against the game" and "as one team"
ask for cooperative. "Head to head" and "against each other" ask for
competitive. A game is cooperative if its mechanics include "Cooperative
Game". Otherwise it is competitive, including teams that play against each
other.

Age. "Our 8-year-old" means the minimum age must be 8 or lower. "Family
game" doesn't tell you the age.

Things to avoid. A game has a feature if its card has the tag, or if the
description shows the feature as part of how the game is played, even in an
optional variant. A tag always counts.
- "No fighting", "no combat": the Fighting category, or players' characters
  or creatures attack, battle or duel other characters or creatures. Armies
  or units attacking on a map are violence, not fighting.
- "Nothing violent": the Wargame category, any fighting, or a game about
  war, raiding, conquest or killing.
- "Nothing scary", "nothing creepy": the Horror or Zombies category, or a
  game meant to frighten, with vampires, zombies, hauntings or being hunted.
  Fantasy monsters and cartoon ghosts alone are not horror.
- "No timers", "no racing against the clock": the Real-time category or
  Real-Time mechanic, or a sand timer, or everyone playing at once as fast
  as they can. "Fast-paced" doesn't count.
- "Nobody knocked out", "nobody sitting out": the Player Elimination
  mechanic, or the description says a player is out and watches while the
  others keep playing.
Figures of speech don't count, such as "battle for points" or "fight over
resources". Judge what actually happens when people play.

HOW TO DECIDE
1. List the requirements in the request, leaving out the wishes.
2. For each game, mark each requirement as meets, breaks or can't tell.
3. Pick a game that meets every requirement. If there is none, decline.
In the explanation, use only facts from the card and the description.

Answer with JSON only, in this form, with the keys in this order:
{"requirements": ["<each requirement in the request, as a short phrase, without the wishes>"],
 "checks": {"A": "<for each requirement: meets, breaks or can't tell, with the fact you used>",
            "B": "...", "C": "...", "D": "...", "E": "..."},
 "pick": <the letter of a game that meets every requirement, in quotes, or null to decline>,
 "explanation": "<one or two sentences for the person>"}

Request:
Me and my three friends play together a lot, and we want something new to try. We only have an hour tops, and we need easy rules. Something similar to Coffee Rush and Popcorn would be nice, where you upgrade your board as you go.

Candidate games:

[A] Fluttering Souls (2019)
Players: 2
Play time: 10 to 20 minutes
Minimum age: 13
Complexity: 1.23 out of 5, from 13 votes
Game types: not listed
Categories: Animals, Card Game
Mechanics: Hand Management, Set Collection
Description:
Fluttering Souls is a captivating, beautifully illustrated two-player game based on the Japanese legend of The White Butterfly. You will compete to collect a kaleidoscope of butterflies in the hope of being visited by The White Butterfly; the soul of a lost loved one.

Legend of the White Butterfly
Many years ago an apprentice merchant named Takahama fell hopelessly in love with a woman named Akiko. They became engaged, but, tragically, Akiko died before they could be wed. 
Takahama was distraught. He had built a life and a successful career, but he could not bear to be away from his love. Such was his dedication to Akiko that he abandoned his trade and gave his life to the upkeep of the cemetery where she was buried. 
For 50 years Takahama visited Akiko’s grave every day with a single pure white rose. One day, Takahama fell so ill he could not go outside. Fearing he may die, his sister and niece came to care for him. While he lay there, unable to move, a butterfly of the purest white landed gently on his pillow. Annoyed, Takahama’s niece tried to shoo the butterfly, but it would not stray from the pillow of the dying man. 
As Takahama’s final breath left his body, so the butterfly flew to the grave of Akiko and disappeared. White butterflies are believed to be the visiting souls of loved ones. Worried that Takahama had not visited her grave that day; Akiko looked over him and did not leave until his soul had joined hers.

Overview
Fluttering Souls is a 2 player game, made up of 3 - 5 rounds. In each round players take turns collecting butterflies to earn victory points, either in a set or by themselves. The player that collects the most victory points at the end of a round is awarded a White Butterfly Token; a visit from a lost loved one. The first player to collect 3 White Butterfly Tokens is the winner.

—description from the publisher

[B] Whale Riders: The Card Game (2021)
Players: 2 to 5
Play time: 20 minutes
Minimum age: 8
Complexity: 1.09 out of 5, from 11 votes
Game types: family
Categories: Card Game, Fantasy
Mechanics: Events, Hand Management, Push Your Luck, Set Collection
Description:
While preparing for the winter, the whale riders were surprised by a sudden drop in temperature. The Ice Coast will freeze early and will make the journey for supplies even more dangerous than usual.

The riders bond together and journey as a group one final time from port to port. Many supplies are needed for their clans, and the riders agree to band together and commit to sharing one big consignment in each port.

Soon, however, it becomes apparent that the raiders’ preferences for the offered consignments differ greatly. In each port, the to-ing and fro-ing begins anew to close the most preferred deal…

In Whale Riders: The Card Game, a reimplementation of Reiner Knizia's classic card game Trendy, you ride alongside others to buy goods along the Ice Coast, sometimes working together with others only to become competitors again when a better proposition comes along.

[C] Monopoly: Wonder of The World (2003)
Players: 2 to 8
Play time: 90 minutes
Minimum age: 8
Complexity: 1.22 out of 5, from 9 votes
Game types: not listed
Categories: Economic, Negotiation
Mechanics: Auction / Bidding, Player Elimination, Roll / Spin and Move, Set Collection, Trading
Description:
The classic real estate game. Buy properties, build houses and hotels, collect rent from fellow players. Repeat as necessary until everyone else is bankrupt.
Build your real estate in wonders of the world.

[D] Blossoms (2018)
Players: 2
Play time: 20 minutes
Minimum age: 8
Complexity: 1.19 out of 5, from 26 votes
Game types: family
Categories: Card Game, Farming
Mechanics: Push Your Luck, Set Collection
Description:
In Blossoms (original title Kwiatki), players compete to create the most beautiful flower bouquet. The longer the flowers, the higher they score!

To set up, give each player two random face-down cards and three action tokens. Place the flower pots in the center of the playing area with space above them for the growing flowers. Place four different flower cards, one in each pot. Take one card from the draw pile and place it aside face-down.

Players alternate taking turns, trying to make the most valuable combination of flowers possible. On their turn, a player can conduct any number of actions, which are:


    Growth — Draw one card from the deck and place it in any pot that has the same flower type.
    Cut — Cut down one pot of flowers to score points; this ends your round.
    Special — Use your action tokens to perform one extra action depending on which pot you choose.


A player's turn ends when they decide to cut flowers, pass, or when they have BAD LUCK. The game ends when the last card from the deck is drawn. Points are then scored by the size and diversity of sets you have planted. Whoever has the higher score wins!

[E] Garden Competition (2004)
Players: 3 to 5
Play time: 60 minutes
Minimum age: 10
Complexity: 2.77 out of 5, from 22 votes
Game types: strategy
Categories: Bluffing, Economic, Farming
Mechanics: Modular Board, Simulation, Tile Placement
Description:
Welcome to the Garden Competition, where you play a neighbourhood student cultivating a garden in the hopes of winning this year’s gardening competition.  Compete against the other players for the favour of your neighbours and for limited flowers at the nursery.

Each player knows some of the flowers and colours the judge is looking for, but no player knows everything the judge is looking for.  Try to guess the parts you don’t know by watching the behaviour of the other players.  The judge also has some secret criteria that only she knows, which you can learn about by taking her out for a cup of coffee.
